verses: قٓ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ
بَلْ عَجِبُوٓا۟ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرٌ مِّنْهُمْ فَقَالَ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا شَىْءٌ عَجِيبٌ
أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا ذَٰلِكَ رَجْعٌۢ بَعِيدٌ
قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ وَعِندَنَا كِتَٰبٌ حَفِيظٌۢ
بَلْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ فَهُمْ فِىٓ أَمْرٍ مَّرِيجٍ
أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا وَزَيَّنَّٰهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجٍ
وَٱلْأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَٰهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۭ بَهِيجٍ
تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُّنِيبٍ
وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً مُّبَٰرَكًا فَأَنۢبَتْنَا بِهِۦ جَنَّٰتٍ وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ
وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَٰتٍ لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ
رِّزْقًا لِّلْعِبَادِ وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِۦ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ
كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
وَعَادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوَٰنُ لُوطٍ
وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ
أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلْأَوَّلِ بَلْ هُمْ فِى لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى ٱلْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ
مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ
وَجَآءَتْ سَكْرَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ بِٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ
وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْوَعِيدِ
وَجَآءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ
لَّقَدْ كُنتَ فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ
وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ هَٰذَا مَا لَدَىَّ عَتِيدٌ
أَلْقِيَا فِى جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ
مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ مُّرِيبٍ
ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِى ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلشَّدِيدِ
قَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ رَبَّنَا مَآ أَطْغَيْتُهُۥ وَلَٰكِن كَانَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۭ بَعِيدٍ
قَالَ لَا تَخْتَصِمُوا۟ لَدَىَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُم بِٱلْوَعِيدِ
مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَىَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِظَلَّٰمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ ٱمْتَلَأْتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ
وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ
هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ
مَّنْ خَشِىَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَجَآءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُّنِيبٍ
ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْخُلُودِ
لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ
وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُم بَطْشًا فَنَقَّبُوا۟ فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُۥ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ
فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ ٱلْغُرُوبِ
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَٰرَ ٱلسُّجُودِ
وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ
يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيْحَةَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْخُرُوجِ
إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْىِۦ وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا ٱلْمَصِيرُ
يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا ذَٰلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ
نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِجَبَّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ

leads.title: Solomon made king; Levites counted, divided and assigned duties ↔ Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Levites stand every morning and evening to thank and praise YHWH (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Solomon made king; Levites counted, divided and assigned duties: Aaron and his sons are set apart forever to burn incense, minister and bless in God's name; The aged king makes his son king during his own lifetime; Levite service counted from twenty years of age by David's last words; With a fixed temple, Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle; Brothers with few sons are counted together as one ancestral house; Moses' sons are reckoned among the Levites, not the priests; Daughters who inherit must marry within their father's tribe so land does not pass away; The king makes the musical instruments used for temple praise; Levites perform sanctuary work from age thirty to fifty; Levites are given wholly to the priest as assistants; God praised morning and evening [divergence between the texts]; Calendar of festivals with prescribed offerings (Passover, Weeks, Trumpets, Atonement, Booths); and 3 more.

Only in Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness: On the day the caller calls from a place near at hand, and they hear the Cry (al-sayha): the day of coming forth; The damned man's companion (qarin) disputes before God: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress'; The earth splits open from them and they hasten forth to the gathering; 'Enter it in peace': the day of eternity; they have what they wish and more (mazid) with God; The Garden is brought near to the God-fearing, not far off; God created the heavens and earth in six days and no weariness (lughub) touched him; Every soul comes with a driver (sa'iq) and a witness (shahid); The stupor (sakra) of death comes with the truth: 'this is what you tried to avoid'; Two receivers sit on the right and the left recording every word a person utters; At judgment the covering is removed from a person and his sight that day is sharp as iron; Four things are never satisfied: Sheol, the barren womb, earth not filled with water, and fire that never says 'Enough'; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

matches.note: The clearest rebuttal of a HB statement in this chunk. Exodus: kî šēšeṯ yāmîm ʿāśâ YHWH ʾeṯ haš-šāmayim wə-ʾeṯ hā-ʾāreṣ û-ḇay-yôm haš-šəḇîʿî šāḇaṯ wa-yyinnāp̄aš. Quran: wa-la-qad khalaqnā s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa wa-mā baynahumā fī sittati ayyāmin wa-mā massanā min lughūb. Same six days (šēšeṯ yāmîm / sittati ayyām) and the same heavens and earth, but instead of 'he rested and caught his breath' the Quran has 'no weariness touched us'. The next verse turns from rest to praise: fa-ṣbir ... wa-sabbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbik (50:39).

leads.title: The valley of dry bones ↔ Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?' (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in The valley of dry bones: God will open his people's graves, bring them up from their graves and bring them to the land of Israel; The exiles say 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off'; The prophet summons the breath (ruah) from the four winds to breathe into the slain so they live; The prophet is set down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones and led around among them; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The revived dead stand on their feet, an exceedingly great army; God will put his own spirit within them and cause them to walk in his statutes; A multitude of dead revived [divergence between the texts]; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; A single cry or rebuke (zajra) and the dead stand looking; and 3 more.

Only in Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples: The companions of al-Rass (the well/pit), a destroyed people; Tall palm trees with spathes of layered dates (tal' nadid) as provision; The unbelievers marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; The people of Tubba' (the Himyarite kings of Yemen) as a destroyed people; God built the sky and adorned it, and it has no rifts (furuj); God was not wearied by creating the heavens and earth (polemic against divine rest); Earth built like a structure with measurements, measuring line, sunk bases and a cornerstone; Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again) [divergence between the texts]; Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth; and 5 more.

أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا ذَٰلِكَ رَجْعٌۢ بَعِيدٌ
